title: df vs du: Why Disk Usage Doesn't Match

scenes.line1: Ever seen 'disk full' but free space?
scenes.line2: Why do df and du disagree?
scenes.say: Ever seen 'disk full' but free space? Why do the df and du commands disagree on disk usage?
Df checks the filesystem for used and free space. Du walks directories and adds up file sizes. They measure disk usage differently.

scenes.title: df, du, and inodes
scenes.say: Df dash h T shows size, used, and filesystem type. Df dash i checks inodes, which are file records. Du dash s h shows total size for a folder.
Df and du disagree when a deleted file is still open, files are hidden under a mount point, or ext four reserves space for root.

scenes.question: Disk full but df -h shows free space?
scenes.wrong: Must be a bug. Try rebooting.
scenes.right: It's likely out of inodes. Check df dash i. Millions of tiny files can fill up inodes even if there's free gigabytes.
scenes.say: If disk is full but df dash h shows free space, it's likely out of inodes. Check df dash i. Millions of tiny files can fill up inodes even if there's free gigabytes.
